brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit (small footprint of bases)
requirements.evidence: 3 full hex bases at 0,0,0 0,1,0 1,0,0 forming minimal L-shaped unit (~3 cells). Compact.
Placed drawer frame notch at 1,1,0 (notch:0#1,1#notch2) between bases; find_sockets for drawer returned 0 offers - no drawer socket available on this configuration. Drawer itself could not be placed.

requirements.requirement: Spike at corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 exists from the three bases and spike socket s66 offered, but final build currently has no spike placed after trial removals due to clash with upper level and platform restrictions.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm and platform-lrg both refused TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED 'this spike cannot carry a platform' for solid/mount variants tried; alternative not offered by configurator.

finish.summary: Built compact 3-base L desk unit with drawer-frame notch; drawer and platform-spike requirements could not be satisfied due to configurator constraints (no drawer offers, platform accessory not allowed on this spike type, spike clash with upper storey).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
